newsitem.title: UK: LME aluminium shaky, but spreads hold up.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium shaky, but spreads hold up.

text.p: Three months aluminium jumped on copper's bearish bandwagon on Monday but spreads were firm ahead of pricing of the August date, traders said.
The key August/September spread was expected to flare in ring activity as shorts covered exposed positions, but later the tightness should start to dissipate, they added.
Three months aluminium slid in pre-market business to $1,663 per tonne, down $39 from Friday's afternoon kerb close, on Far Eastern selling and long liquidation.
It was partly a delayed reaction to heavy losses on Friday in copper, which hit six-month lows and went into contango.
Selling was first seen early on Monday in Asia, which missed out on copper's rout on Friday, renewing pressure on the whole complex.
Chartists pegged good support in aluminium at $1,660, just above the 30-day moving average. "If we can hold above $1,660, we should be looking at higher prices," a trader said.
Below there, a further floor was seen at $1,615/20.
In ring trading, cash was expected to be bid up as shorts scrambled to cover positions. "I wouldn't be surprised to see August/September at $40/$50 (backwardation)," a trader said.
But the positions were expected to be covered, not rolled over, so the tightness could start to ease in the afternoon, he added.
The cash/threes spread was indicated on Monday morning at a $30/$35 backwardation, barely changed from Friday evening.
Aluminium stocks rose by 6,650 tonnes as more metal was attracted by the backwardation, traders said.
The renewed pressure sent copper prices sulking to a low of $2,168, a loss of $45 from Friday's kerb close.
The near-term target was $2,150, traders said.
"Once it hits $2,150, I wouldn't be surprised to see some buying come in," one said.
But with stocks continuing to rise and the market in contango, more weakness was expected in the medium term.
Inventories increased by 3,725 tonnes on Monday and the cash/threes was indicated at a $3/$5 contango.
Zinc also felt the chill, dropping $25 to a low of $1,500, even though stocks fell by 3,125 tonnes.
But the uptrend remained intact and the market was expected to bounce back as spreads remained firm.
The cash/threes was indicated at a $150/$155 backwardation, little changed from Friday.
Other metals, which had already seen major losses recently, were less affected.
Nickel dipped $50 to $6,580, keeping above last week's low of $6,520, while lead added $1 to $616.
Tin also was marginally higher at $5,400, up $20, and aluminium alloy held little changed at $1,512 versus $1,505/15.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
